title: Back with Henderson: the Harvest Moon Ball in Central Park
summary: Henderson's band was reorganized in 1935. Thomas describes the free Harvest Moon Ball with Abe Lyman, crowds of 100,000 rushing the bandstand, and the move to Madison Square Garden.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Now, who's place did you take when you went back with Smack Fletcher ?
Well, the band was being reorganized.
Oh, that's right.
It's got to be '35. Give me, allow a liar for a year or two, '35.
Yes, that's right. The summer of '35 until '37.

I saw the damnedest thing happen I've ever seen in my life. They had a thing called the Harvest Moon Ball. That was in Central Park on the Mall so they had selected two bands and our band, Henderson said Our band, you know. I still say it was our band because (everyone was after the) Duke and (when we get) the Duke ...
I mean Fletcher was still the biggest.

Oh, are you kidding. Well, nobody was any bigger. We wanted to get to the Duke. ... and '35 and they had the Harvest Moon Ball. Of course, it was free and Ed Sullivan was m.c. at that time. So they had two bands, Henderson's band, our band, and Abe Lyman's band. Now I've seen a lot of things happen in a lot of ways. Sometimes you say ... there were 100,000 people out there. I didn't count them and we struck up the, thought we'd play a little music there, you know, and, Stanley Dance... ... that's the most frightening thing I've ever seen. The people
JT ( 1 of 2) 13

were rushing to hear the music. Ain't that something. It's almost unbelievable, isn't it? And, we didn't finish a tune. In fact, we didn't finish a phrase because the people were so happy to hear what we were trying to do.
Really? He was that popular at that time?

Stan, there must have been 100,000 people. They said 100,000, I said it looked like more than that to me. And, after that they took us to, after the first August Moon Ball, they took us to the Garden, Madison Square Garden and started charging admission.
Oh, this was free in Central Park?

Oh, yes. But, the surprising thing about music and all those things that happened in those days, we played to crowds of 2,000. We played to Milwaukee, 7,000 in one place and 3,000 one night and Ellington came to town. And they have a place out there called, I can't remember all those things, anyhow, ? had been there. I think he had drawn something like 19,000 people.
And where was this, Joe?
Milwaukee.
You were out there once with Smack ?
No, no, I meant Abernathy.
We've gone back.
JT (1 of 2)
Well, you know, reminisce in tempo.

I think Duke has drawn something like 70. He's drawn 17,000. He had three bands. Now you think of these 100,000 people so they put it in Madison Square Garden. And that was the first Haywest Moon Ball. I think that was Henderson in '35 and I may be a liar for a couple of years.
Was this one in Central Park was opposite Abe Lyman anyway?
Yes. I think Abe Lyman's band but I think we did the same thing in Madison Square Garden.
Well, did the people dance at this ball?

Well, no, I'll tell you what happened. The August Moon Ball is for the people from the different ideas of dance there and these were cats who would dance the waltz, you know, and the cats who would do cats who would dance the tango and the dance this kind of thing and out of that came a group called Whitey and his Lindy Hoppers. So we played for the Lindy hoppers, and Abe Lyman played for the waltzers and we played the tango and all that kind of thing. It was a very enjoyable thing. Those pictures I can't find them. I must have given them, loan out idea. Snack had a tremendous idea about musicianship. He was strict. He was very much like Mr. Langford.
